narrative: Material PL2__M4A82400 exhibits erratic demand with CV=1.00 across 241 working days, with 73.9% of days recording positive demand. Lead times are extremely short on average (0.44 days) but highly unstable (CV=1.07). The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: a safety stock of 88,873 units provides the 95% service level target, while the EOQ-derived order quantity of 40,689 units (above the 28,031 MOQ) balances ordering and holding costs. Storage capacity is ample at only 10.9% utilisation.
warnings: 3 outliers detected and winsorized at 99th percentile
High demand variability (CV=1.00) — consider advanced forecasting methods
Unstable lead times (CV=1.07) — consider supplier development or lead-time contracts
Optimised policy has higher total annual cost (+$86,335) due to safety stock investment required for 95% service level; trade-off is explicit and justified

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review reorder-point policy with EOQ
research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand (CV=1.00, 74% active days) with very short but unstable lead times suits a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The combined-variance safety stock formula captures both demand and lead-time uncertainty. EOQ exceeds MOQ so no MOQ constraint binds. Gamma distribution approximation is consistent with right-skewed, non-negative demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: CV close to 1.0 with lead-time instability means safety stock could be understated in extreme disruption scenarios. Robust IQR-based safety stock (113,271 units) provides an upper bound and should be considered if service level breaches are costly. Storage capacity is not a binding constraint.
